_what: The door's generic read of an account's own records, and what a Workshop tool run may be granted at it (src/record_value/account_routes.rs, src/account_rights/run_capability.rs). At `resource`, the `read` operation answers one record {id, type, value} for input {id, type?, at?}: value null when the record is absent or, with type given, of another kind. With `at` (an ISO time, or whole milliseconds since 1970), it answers the record as it was saved at that moment (src/record_value/history.rs read_at, the record store's record_at; old trillion record-log-store.mjs recordAt): {id, type, value, version, saved_at, complete, kept_from}, value null when there was no live version then; `complete` is false when the versions that could answer have left the store, and `kept_from` is then the earliest time the answer is good for. It is read under the same rights as the plain read. The `list` operation answers a page {records: [{id, type, value}], next} for input {type, order?, prefix?, above?, below?, reverse?, limit?, after?, fields?, where?, view?}: `order` names a declared record store order (src/storage/record_store/settings.json `orders`) covering type, else the type's ids greatest first (reverse must then be true); prefix/above/below bound the order's ECMA JSON values (ids when no order); limit is a positive whole number (`list_page` when absent); the door scans at most 1000 order positions or ids in one answer (with `where`, at most `where_walk_most`) and returns `next` to continue, so a caller can request any page size without materializing the kind; `after` is a previous page's `next`; `fields` (at most 64 top-level field names) narrows each row's value to those fields and an empty list leaves ids and types alone, so a page of rows a caller reads only some of holds many more of them; `where` (an object of at most 64 top-level field names) shows only the rows whose opened value holds each named field equal, as JSON, to the value given, and `limit` then bounds the rows shown: the answer reads on through the whole list, up to `where_walk_most` positions, until `limit` rows match, so a row that matches far down a large list is found in one call, with `next` continuing after the last row read; a `where` with no `order`, `prefix`, `above` or `below` of its own uses a declared record store order that lists the kind by a field it names (an order whose first path is that top-level field, or `stored` then it; the rows the order holds for that value are the run of equal values, so a page costs the rows that match, not the kind), and when no field it names has an order it reads the kind row by row and continues by cursor, even when the kind is large; `view: true` reads the kind as a typed table: the page adds `schema` ({fields: {name: text|number|boolean|list|json}, indexes}, null when the kind has no schema history) and each row adds `fields` (every schema field: its value, or null) and `mismatched` (the fields whose stored value has another type than the schema's, read as null and never coerced) beside the whole `value`, read after the record was opened (sealed fields, erasure), and a `fields` projection keeps both; a page is cut to the leading rows whose answer fits one MCP message (`next` then continues after the last row shown, even when fewer than `limit` rows are shown), and a record, or a first row, larger than one message is answered as pages of its own bytes: a `byte_page` answer {total, blake3, offset, length, base64, next_after_byte} (the record's answer, or a list's or history's first row as a page of one row), and the same call with `after_byte` (a page's `next_after_byte`) answers the page from there; `total` and `blake3` are of the whole answer on every page, so a reader joins the pages, checks them and parses the answer it would have had (`workspace:read` answers its first record the same way, its `after_byte` input beside `after`). No record is refused for its size; an `after_byte` past the answer's end is an input refusal. The `history` operation answers a record's version history, newest first, for input {id, before_version?, limit}: {versions: [{version, value, deleted, at}], next}, where `at` is the ISO time the version was written, `deleted` versions have a null value, `before_version` keeps only versions below it, `next` is the next page's before_version (null at the oldest), and `limit` is 1..`history_max` (required). History is not in `run_operations`: it names no kind, so a tool run cannot be granted it. The `outside_choices` operation reports what a list definition's change left behind: for input {list, limit?, after?} (`list` the definition's record id) it scans the rows of the kind the definition declares, by id greatest first, and answers {kind, scanned, rows_outside, outside: [{id, field, value}], next} for the rows whose value in a choice field is outside that field's declared choices (an array is checked per element; null fits); `limit` is 1..999, `list_page` when absent; at most 1000 order positions or ids are walked in one answer, and the page is cut to the rows whose answer fits one message, with `next` continuing after the last scanned position or row (null once every row was scanned). A definition that declares no choices answers kind null and nothing outside; an absent list record is an input refusal. A change to a list definition is never blocked by rows outside its choices (a write of a value outside them is refused, but a row already holding one stays writable); this read is how the person sees them. It is not in `run_operations` either. What an MCP initialize answer carries to a connecting AI is the rows of the list the installed Workshop declares itself: the one Workshop folder whose rows file holds a row of kind `instructions.row_kind` names its list file in that row's `file` (src/tool_runs/tools/instruction_file.rs; src/mcp/instructions.rs reads it), so the engine names no Workshop folder, among them the standing job a person's own AI picks up on connecting, so work a wake fired (an ai-job record) reaches it with no runner. All three open every record through record_value::read (sealed fields, erasure). `run_operations` are the door operations a tool row may declare (invoke.records.rights[]: {kind, operations, id? or prefix?}), each with the rule of what one call touches: `items`, the path to its items (`*` is every item of an array; none is the input itself); in each item `kind`, the field naming its kind; `id`, the field naming its record id, or `id_prefix`, the field naming the start of the ids it reaches (absent means every id of the kind; not when the item names `id_prefix_unless`, an order, whose range is over values); and `value`, the field a write carries; and `every_kind`, on a read only, the text that stands for every kind the person holds: records:search with no `type` (every kind but those that stay on this computer) is covered only by a right {kind: "*", operations: ["records:search"]}, a read-only search right over every kind; a right naming that text with any other operation, an id or a prefix is refused when the row is read, so it never widens a write, and a search naming `type` "*" is refused. At a run's capability every item must name its kind (and the id its rule needs) and be covered by a declared right of that operation: a right with `id` covers only that id, with `prefix` only ids (or id prefixes) that start with it, without either the whole kind. A run whose capability carries a wake cause has that cause stamped into every written value (wake.json `cause_field`), and a record it removes (a removal carries no stamp) is named to wake by the door right after the write commits (src/wake.rs Waker::own_change), so the run's own removal wakes nothing. records:write is the shipped write (own-record-writes.json); `workspace:write` is the workspace write ({writes: [{address_label, payload, expected_identity?, scope_id?}], conflict_policy?}, src/local_account/native_command_context/workspace_write.rs), granted like `workspace:read` by a right whose kind is `resource` and whose `id` is one exact label: every item of `writes` must name a label a right of that operation covers, and a `resolve_conflict` call (it names no label) is never granted to a run; `sharing.receive` (src/account_rights/share-given.json `receive_operation`, input {door, label, key} or {door, label, on: false}) is granted by a right whose kind is `resource`, over every share the person was given (its rule names no kind or id), so a Workshop tool the person's screen runs can keep the key they pasted, which goes only into their vault; a row's invoke.records.most_writes may lower its per-write limit; inside its transaction a run's write also may not replace or remove a record of a kind it was not granted. `wake.switch` turns one of a tool's declared wakes on or off for input {tool, id, on} (src/wake.rs Waker::switch): switched on, the switch records the party that wrote it (src/account/account_routes.rs SignIn::party_of: its cause name, never a credential), whose live rights ∩ the row's invoke.records each run it starts gets at that moment (src/account_rights/run_cause.rs); switched off, the wake stops. Nothing else is kept. `wake.causes` answers what the person's causes screen shows, one page for input {} and the page after it for {after}, a page's `next` (src/wake.rs Waker::causes: the engine's now_ms, the declared wakes of the page, the book's marks of them, its live causes without their inputs on the first page, each watched resource's newest stamp, and `next`, null on the last page); a page holds as many wakes as fit one MCP answer. A run may be granted them by a rights item {wakes: "*" or a tool id, operations}: a switch names its tool, so a tool id covers that tool's wakes; the causes read covers every tool's, so only "*" grants it. Their rules name no kind, so the domain is this door's resource. A list's field definition may carry `needs_person_present_to_set: [values]`: a write that newly sets one of those values in a row, or that narrows, removes or moves that mark, is refused with `needs_person_present` naming the record, field and value unless the caller's own sign-in pass was issued within Better Auth's fresh-session age (src/account/person_present.rs, src/account/signed_in/settings.json `fresh_age_seconds`); the person renews it by signing in again (a passkey re-authentication). A request never says the person is present itself.
_result_read: Protected result recovery for the original record command: input {request_key,operation,input} carries its ORIGINAL key, declared write operation and unchanged input; the outer delivery key is separate. The native command-journal owner rechecks the same account/principal/workspace, original input and result scopes; tool runs narrow the reconstructed original write before recovery and output. Missing, incomplete or erased journal state remains UNKNOWN/refused; this operation never executes an effect or reports an absent result as no effect. It is separate from ordinary logical reads and has no independent generic run grant; its native handler owns the original-operation authorization.
_current_read_identity: A successful current records:read adds identity, the opaque current root revision/stamp token from that same admitted logical read before computed fields. Pass unchanged as expected:{type,identity} on records:write for that same id. It fences the root only, not shared children or computed fields. It is text, never a number or content hash. Historical at reads, absent and wrong-type results do not return a current identity.

search._what: One question over every record the account keeps (src/record_value/search.rs, the port of old trillion src/search.mjs `finish` and its words-in-records lane, reached as the old MCP `search` tool reached GET /namespace/search). At `resource`, `operation` answers {question, terms, results: [{id, source, kind_label, type, title, name, record, address: {resource, operation, input}, found_in, places: [{place, said}], said, score}], unavailable, pending} for input {question, type?, limit?}: the question cut to `question_chars`, its distinct words of at least `min_word_length` letters; candidates are the records the record store word index (src/storage/record_store/segments.rs, fed by every write) holds for every uncommon asked word (a word with `word_hits` postings is common and narrows nothing; a word no record holds answers nothing), each opened and kept only when every asked word starts a word of its text; each kind is one lane, ranked by reciprocal rank fusion with `k`; `said` is the words around the first asked word, cut to `said_characters`; `address` is the read that opens the record. `limit` is 1..`most` (`limit` when absent). With `type` only that kind is answered (and a run may be granted it for that kind); with none, a run needs the read-only right over every kind, {kind: "*", operations: ["records:search"]}; with none, every kind but those that stay on this computer. It answers records only: the one search over records and files together is a Workshop tool, which merges this answer with the account files' `search` by rank.

_homes: Where a kind's records live when they are not in the account's primary store (src/native_boot/mcp_local.rs to_kinds_home). A kind whose name starts with one of `kinds` may have a home: the row `<row_prefix><kind>` in the primary, whose value names the record domain that holds its records ({kind, scope: {id, incarnation, generation}}). A records call that names no scope and one such kind is answered in that domain. Old trillion src/placed-lists.mjs invariant 1: one store answers for a list's rows, its home.
_old_paths: The paths old trillion's signed-in page called for one record (Trillion-X/trillion tag old-trillion-before-worker-retire src/own-resource-compatibility.mjs:276-277: GET /records/<id> was the `records:read` command {id}, the id percent-decoded), each answered by this door's operation of that name with the input as the old route took it, read by src/account_files/page_paths.rs as the account files door reads its own (src/account_files/account-files-routes.json `_old_paths` says the row shape). `unless` keeps the exact paths old trillion answered by another owner before this one (src/worker.mjs:1014-1020 /records/conflicts, :1224 /records/model; src/own-resource-compatibility.mjs:265-273 /records/history, /records/turns, /records/document-operations), so none of them is read as a record id. The page's session admits each call (Door::page_call); the owner route that sends these paths to this door is src/server/owner-routes.json's row of this resource.

references._what: The bounded reverse read of declared model parts. Input {id,type?,role?,limit?,after?}; type narrows holders. It answers {records:[{id,type,via}],coverage:{index_complete,complete,pagination,consistent_snapshot},next}. Each candidate is opened under the current logical read, and local-only kinds are omitted from remote answers. The caller must retain ordinary records-read authority for target/root and all holders. It grants no file content authority. Whole-holder cursors are encrypted with a process-local key and bound to the account/sign-in, target, type, role and limit; restart invalidates a cursor. Raw examined counts and unreadable holder identities are never disclosed. There is one bounded index page including lookahead, no body scan or index writes. Completeness stays false while model backfill is pending. Not in run_operations: a run cannot grant both target and discovered-holder read scopes through a single input rule yet. The generic record store parts index replaces the retired scope-links owner.
